newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon raises CVRD weight.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon raises CVRD weight.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it raised miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce's weight in its model Latin American portfolio, scratching state-owned Petrobras BR Distribuidora to make room.

"To make room for CVRD in our model Latin America portfolio, we are selling our stake in Petrobras BR and taking its weight down from 2.3 percent to zero," Salomon analyst John Mullin said in a report.
Salomon raised its recommended weighting for CVRD preferred to 2.6 percent from 0.6 percent in its previous Latin American model, he said.
The brokerage's neutral benchmark weight for CVRD preferred is 1.7 percent and 0.2 percent for oil distributor Petrobras BR preferred is 1.7 percent, he added.

Mullin said the move follows Salomon analyst Mauricio Reveco's upgrade of his investment recommendation on CVRD to buy from hold. Reveco also raised his CVRD earnings estimates to $1.61 per share from $1.49 for 1997 and to $1.84 from $1.66 a share in 1998.

"Mauricio believes that CVRD's positives outweigh the risks at the present time and that CVRD's shares are a good investment vehicle to benefit from earnings growth in the natural resources industry," Mullin said.
He said Petrobras BR's price has risen 53 percent so far this year, making the company more expensive relative to its peers.
